questions.q: The editorial says we should answer a remark about our faults as we answer a mirror. What does that mean?
options: Return the remark in kind
Not quite. The article says: Accept it without taking offence and put the matter right.
Ask for a second opinion
Not quite. The article says: Accept it without taking offence and put the matter right.
Accept it without taking offence and put the matter right
Yes. Taking offence is the great obstacle to learning.
Look away from it
Not quite. The article says: Accept it without taking offence and put the matter right.
questions.rationale: “When a mirror tells you have dirt on your face, you don’t get angry. Rather, you will accept it as true and promptly wash your face.”

questions.q: What happens to a tree that is dug up and replanted again and again, and what does the article compare this to?
options: It flowers sooner – like a person who learns quickly
Not quite. The article says: Its roots shorten until it cannot grow – like a person who keeps changing his place and never builds a history.
Nothing changes – place does not matter
Not quite. The article says: Its roots shorten until it cannot grow – like a person who keeps changing his place and never builds a history.
It grows stronger – like a person who travels widely
Not quite. The article says: Its roots shorten until it cannot grow – like a person who keeps changing his place and never builds a history.
Its roots shorten until it cannot grow – like a person who keeps changing his place and never builds a history
Right. Stability is the condition of growth.
questions.rationale: “A person who frequently changes his place of work is one who has had a ‘break in his history’… a person without a history is like a rootless tree.”

questions.q: Which saying of the Prophet does the article quote in support of constancy?
options: “Seek knowledge even if far away”
Not quite. The article says: “The best deeds are those which are done regularly, even if they are small”.
“The best deeds are those which are done regularly, even if they are small”
Correct.
“Actions are judged by intentions”
Not quite. The article says: “The best deeds are those which are done regularly, even if they are small”.
“Tie your camel, then trust in God”
Not quite. The article says: “The best deeds are those which are done regularly, even if they are small”.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet of Islam said: ‘The best deeds are those which are done regularly, even if they are small’ (Ibn Majah).”

questions.q: The article says one group “keeps the markets of the world turning over” while another “turns over new pages in human history.” What marks the second group?
options: They work for a worthwhile cause without seeking reward or credit
Yes. They remember responsibilities, not rights.
They are more highly educated
Not quite. The article says: They work for a worthwhile cause without seeking reward or credit.
They work alone
Not quite. The article says: They work for a worthwhile cause without seeking reward or credit.
They are better paid
Not quite. The article says: They work for a worthwhile cause without seeking reward or credit.
questions.rationale: “Those who are destined to perform great deeds in life are those who do not seek reward for what they have done; the very fact that they have done something is sufficient reward for them.”

questions.q: Some hold that the Quran discourages friendship with people of other faiths. How does the article read the verses cited (60:1, 60:4)?
options: They apply to all people at all times
Not quite. The article says: They concerned a particular wartime incident, not relations in times of peace.
They were addressed to other communities
Not quite. The article says: They concerned a particular wartime incident, not relations in times of peace.
They forbid only business dealings
Not quite. The article says: They concerned a particular wartime incident, not relations in times of peace.
They concerned a particular wartime incident, not relations in times of peace
Well reasoned. Relations with others rest on the laws of peace.
questions.rationale: “What is stated in this chapter… applies for times when war prevails between the followers of Islam and others and not when peace has been established.”

questions.q: Newton lost his father before birth and grew up largely alone. What does the article draw from his story?
options: Children do better without parents
Not quite. The article says: Even hard experiences hold a plus point – his solitude made him a deep thinker.
Even hard experiences hold a plus point – his solitude made him a deep thinker
Yes. “This world is a world of hope.”
Genius is inherited
Not quite. The article says: Even hard experiences hold a plus point – his solitude made him a deep thinker.
Unhappy people cannot succeed
Not quite. The article says: Even hard experiences hold a plus point – his solitude made him a deep thinker.
questions.rationale: “No matter what experiences we go through—even seemingly negative ones—there is always a positive aspect or plus point contained in them.”

questions.article: Has the Age of Oppression Returned?
questions.q: Urged to join the fighting among Muslims of his day, Abdullah ibn Umar refused. What reason did he give?
options: God had forbidden him to shed his brother’s blood; the fighting of the Prophet’s day had been to end persecution, which was over
Right. He would not fight to create strife.
He was too old to fight
Not quite. The article says: God had forbidden him to shed his brother’s blood; the fighting of the Prophet’s day had been to end persecution, which was over.
He supported the other side
Not quite. The article says: God had forbidden him to shed his brother’s blood; the fighting of the Prophet’s day had been to end persecution, which was over.
He was waiting for a better leader
Not quite. The article says: God had forbidden him to shed his brother’s blood; the fighting of the Prophet’s day had been to end persecution, which was over.
questions.rationale: “God prevents me from doing so, for He has forbidden me from spilling my brother’s blood… In the Prophet’s day we fought until there was no more oppression.”

questions.q: How does the article describe the duty of an ordinary person, as against a ruler, with regard to justice?
options: The ordinary person must enforce justice on the ruler
Not quite. The article says: An ordinary person must act and speak justly in his own sphere; one given authority must also establish a just system.
Both must set up courts
Not quite. The article says: An ordinary person must act and speak justly in his own sphere; one given authority must also establish a just system.
An ordinary person must act and speak justly in his own sphere; one given authority must also establish a just system
Yes. Responsibility follows capacity.
Neither is responsible for justice
Not quite. The article says: An ordinary person must act and speak justly in his own sphere; one given authority must also establish a just system.
questions.rationale: “The responsibility of an ordinary person… is to act justly at all times within the sphere in which he operates. But someone whom God has blessed with authority must… also establish a just system.”

questions.q: From Adam’s eating of the forbidden fruit, what weakness of man does the article say Satan learnt to exploit?
options: Wanting the whole and not being content with a part – which leads to ingratitude
Exactly. In this world no one is given everything.
Love of sleep
Not quite. The article says: Wanting the whole and not being content with a part – which leads to ingratitude.
Fear of the unknown
Not quite. The article says: Wanting the whole and not being content with a part – which leads to ingratitude.
Forgetfulness of names
Not quite. The article says: Wanting the whole and not being content with a part – which leads to ingratitude.
questions.rationale: “Man, because of his disposition, will want the whole, and will not be content with only a part of it… As a result, mankind forever lives in ingratitude.”

questions.q: What does the article say about a person who, when an opportunity is already before him, keeps praying for one?
options: He should stop praying altogether
Not quite. The article says: It is like asking for sunshine while the sun is shining; the moment calls for thanks and use of what is given.
It is like asking for sunshine while the sun is shining; the moment calls for thanks and use of what is given
Well read. Opportunity comes unannounced.
He shows admirable persistence
Not quite. The article says: It is like asking for sunshine while the sun is shining; the moment calls for thanks and use of what is given.
His prayer will bring a better opportunity
Not quite. The article says: It is like asking for sunshine while the sun is shining; the moment calls for thanks and use of what is given.
questions.rationale: “When a person gets an opportunity and instead of recognizing it and utilizing it, he prays for an opportunity from God, he is going against the law of nature. Such a moment is a moment of being thankful to God.”
